title: How much profit in a week?
description: Jia buys notebooks at a wholesale price and sells each one for thirty rupees. The profit on one notebook is found by taking away, and the profit on fifty notebooks by writing it over ten and multiplying, the same way as the pens in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: profit on one is selling price minus buying price, and the profit on many is that profit multiplied by the number sold, done through tenths. Watch for students who multiply the buying price instead of the profit.

source: Jia purchases notebooks at a wholesale price of ₹23.6 per piece and sells each notebook at ₹30. How much profit does Jia make if Jia sells 50 books in a week?
video_script.why: The child has multiplied a decimal price by a whole number through fractions and now first finds a profit on one item and then the profit on many.
video_script.substitution: the book's notebooks bought at twenty three point six rupees and sold at thirty rupees, fifty in a week
video_script.anchor: Jia buys notebooks at twenty three point six rupees each, sells each at thirty rupees, and sells fifty in a week
video_script.payoff_line: The profit for the week is now known.
maths_rules: profit on one notebook = selling price − buying price = 30 − 23.6 = 6.4 rupees
size check: 6 × 50 = 300, and 6.4 is a little more than 6, so the profit is a little more than 300
video_script.design: One idea: profit on one item is found by taking away, and tenths multiply like a fraction over ten. Assumes tenths and the idea of profit. The notebooks and the prices stay all video; the total profit appears only on the answer beat.
